title: Add tenant-aware Helm preflight checks and operator quiesce for safer upgrades
author: Maya Thompson
description: Motivation: We've seen a small number of private deployment upgrades fail when tenant workloads (replicas, long-running jobs, or in-progress schema migrations) contend with control-plane changes. This PR introduces tenant-aware preflight checks in the Helm chart + a graceful operator quiesce API to reduce upgrade blast radius and prevent partial upgrades that require manual intervention. Summary of changes: 1) Helm hooks: add preflight "tenant-check" hook that validates: a) no active schema migrations (Postgres migration lock probe), b) no >5 long-running jobs per tenant (k8s Job/PodAge probe), c) KV-cache warm state exists for active routes if configured. 2) Installer CLI: new --quiesce-window flag and a quiesce handshake flow that calls the operator quiesce endpoint to pause write-heavy background jobs and drain autoscaling buffers. 3) Operator: implement /quiesce and /resume REST endpoints (idempotent, tenant-scoped) with RBAC checks and a graceful drain that emits events and exposes metrics (quiesce_duration_seconds, tenants_quiesced_total). 4) Backup verification: installer now validates an on-cluster snapshot exists and a checksum matches a pre-upgrade snapshot manifest; fails fast with instructions when missing. 5) Rollback safety: version-pin file added to helm/templates to prevent accidental mixed-version podsets; installer performs a canary PVC snapshot test before applying new chart values. 6) Docs and runbook: add upgrade playbook section for Private deployments explaining quiesce choreography and troubleshoot steps. Checklist: - [x] Add helm preflight hook and templates - [x] Implement operator quiesce/resume endpoints - [x] Installer CLI flag and handshake + unit tests - [x] Snapshot checksum verifier and PVC canary test - [x] Update docs and runbook - [x] Add e2e smoke test that exercises quiesce and resume How this mitigates risk: preflight prevents upgrades when tenants are mid-migration or when backups are stale; operator quiesce reduces background work to minimize state churn during rollout; PVC canary snapshot ensures restoreability for the most common volume-backed components. Rollout plan: merge to main, feature-flag off by default. Enable for a single pilot customer via a bootstrap flag; observe metrics for 72hrs, then enable wider. Related work: builds on ENG-1812 (snapshot signing) and ENG-1659 (staged tenant backups).

discussion: Aaron: Please add metrics for number of paused tasks and a way to force-resume if the operator is unhealthy. Maya: Added tenants_quiesced_total and quiesce_duration_seconds metrics, and an emergency --force-resume flag on the installer (requires RBAC). Sofia: Noted potential race between Helm hooks and operator rollout; requested a 30s backoff and retry loop in the installer handshake. Maya: Added backoff with exponential jitter and documented the behavior. Dmitri: Ran e2e locally and hit intermittent failure on PVC canary on older k8s versions; added compatibility check and fallback to a dry-run snapshot check. Aaron: CI flake in e2e (timing); re-ran and passed.
release_notes: Added tenant-aware Helm preflight checks, operator quiesce/resume endpoints, snapshot verification and PVC canary test to reduce upgrade failures in Private deployments. Feature gated and disabled by default; see docs/private/upgrade-runbook.md for roll-out steps.
notes_for_oncall: If a customer reports upgrades stuck at 'preflight' step: 1) Check helm hook logs (kubectl get jobs -n <ns>), 2) Confirm snapshot manifest checksum matches S3/GCS manifest, 3) If operator quiesce is stuck, use installer --force-resume with caution, then collect operator logs and /metrics endpoint for tenants_quiesced_total and quiesce_duration_seconds.
tests: Unit tests added for quiesce handlers and snapshot verifier; e2e smoke test exercises full quiesce->upgrade->resume path against kind and GKE; CI pipeline adds a new 'preflight' job that runs the helm hook templates against a dry-run cluster.
